## Background

The users using the scanning electron microscope (SEM) need to manually estimate the height of their mounted samples and enter that height electronically into the microscope settings before they place it in the microscope. This process requires the user to visually compare the sample against a ruler, which is likely inconsistent for the most part, causing inaccurate measurements. Inaccurate height inputs can possibly lead to collisions when inside the microscope chamber, causing damage to the sensitive detectors or possibly limiting its performance.
The client wants a height measurement solution that allows trained users to quickly, safely, and accurately determine the maximum sample height for any standard SEM sample holder. The solution must be able to accommodate all existing holder bases, which have at most a 10 cm radius and sample diameters of 26 mm, while providing readouts with a tolerance of 0.5 mm without contacting the surface of the sample [1]. Additionally, it is very important that nothing touches the top of the sample during the measuring process [2]. The top of the sample is covered in a conductive coating that is on the scale of nanometers thick [2]. Therefore, anything that brushes along the top of the sample could cause damage to the coating and sample itself [1,2]. The solution should be simple to use, highly durable, easily cleaned, minimized the need for calibration while allowing trained non-specialist users to get accurate measurements in under two minutes. The measurement process must be quick in order to make it more convenient for the user because this step should be a relatively simple step in the entire process of using the electron microscope.

## Contributions

- Designed a precision rack and pinion Z-axis measurement system achieving less than 1mm accuracy for SEM sample preparation
- Integrated a laser and photosensor along with a slew bearing for radial motion to detect the tallest point on samples of variable height
- Optimized durability through full material and fatigue analysis, selecting powder nylon (SLS nylon) for superior wear resistance, strength, and dimensional stability under high cycle use
- Delivered a scalable, easily replicable design that improves SEM workflow safety and prevents $1000+ in potential equipment damage from improper sample height
